gravfield.d.M1: Mass of body 1 in Earth masses (Earth = 1)
gravfield.d.M2: Mass of body 2 in Earth masses (Moon = 0.0123)
gravfield.d.two: Show body 2; off gives the field of a single mass
gravfield.d.view: Draw the gravitational field as grid arrows, field lines, or both
gravfield.d.eq: Equipotentials at equal steps $\Delta\Phi$ (dashed) and the one through the point where $g = 0$ (thick, solid)
gravfield.goal.field: Gravitational field: the gravitational force per unit mass on a test mass at each point, $\vec g = \vec F/m$. The field of several masses is the vector sum of the fields of each
gravfield.goal.phi: Gravitational potential $\Phi = -\sum GM_i/r_i$ (zero at infinity), $\vec g = -\nabla\Phi$: the field is perpendicular to the equipotentials and points towards lower $\Phi$
gravfield.obs.drag: Drag the masses $M_1$, $M_2$ and the test mass $m$. The thin arrows $\vec g_1$, $\vec g_2$ add up to the thick arrow $\vec g$; the numbers are in the Σ panel
gravfield.obs.null: At the × the field is zero: the two fields are equal in size and opposite. The point lies closer to the lighter mass, $r_1/r_2 = \sqrt{M_1/M_2}$ (Earth–Moon: 9.0 : 1, $3.46\times10^5$ km from the Earth)
gravfield.obs.eight: The equipotential through the point where $g = 0$ (thick, solid) is a figure eight. Deeper equipotentials enclose each mass separately, shallower ones enclose both
gravfield.obs.perp: Field lines and grid arrows cross the equipotentials at right angles everywhere. Moving along an equipotential, gravity does no work
gravfield.obs.single: One mass (switch off the second mass): $g \propto 1/r^2$ (twice as far → a quarter of $g$), and the equipotentials are concentric circles whose spacing grows outwards ($\Phi \propto -1/r$)
gravfield.obs.analogy: Compare with the electric field: the same inverse-square law ($F = Gm_1m_2/r^2$ vs $F = k\lvert q_1q_2\rvert/r^2$). Gravity only attracts, so field lines only end on masses (the same shape as an arrangement of negative charges only). As between two like charges, there is a point of zero field between the masses
gravfield.as.units: Length unit $10^5$ km $= 10^8$ m, mass unit the Earth mass $M_\oplus = 5.97\times10^{24}$ kg, $G = 6.674\times10^{-11}\ \mathrm{N\,m^2/kg^2}$ (real values). The default layout is the Earth and the Moon: $3.84\times10^5$ km apart, mass ratio 81.3
gravfield.as.point: The masses are fixed point masses (the discs are not to scale; their size grows with the cube root of the mass). The test mass is too small to change the field. $\hat r_i$ is the unit vector from $M_i$ to the point
gravfield.as.plane: The picture is the plane through the masses: a cut through the 3D inverse-square field. The field is that of masses at rest (the Earth–Moon orbital motion and its centrifugal effect are not included)
gravfield.as.arrows: Grid arrow length is a log scale of the field strength (over three decades); the direction is exact. The arrows $\vec g_1$, $\vec g_2$, $\vec g$ at the test mass share a linear scale set by the largest
gravfield.as.eq: Equipotential spacing $\Delta\Phi$: a 1-2-5 step set by the heavier mass (0.5 MJ/kg for one Earth mass). The number of field lines is proportional to the mass (24 on the heavier mass, at least 1 on the lighter)
